sources.title: Carl de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines, revised edition
sources.locator: Complete 366-page book PDF fetched and inspected. Chapter X, printed pp. 123–126 / PDF pp. 139–143: BVALUE's nonempty-span localization, local coefficient reduction and final order-one value. Chapter XI, printed pp. 135–138 / PDF pp. 152–155: single-knot insertion, refined controls, preservation and convex-hull discussion. Chapter IV, printed pp. 43–45 / PDF pp. 60–62: complete/clamped and natural endpoint conditions. Chapter V, printed pp. 51–57 / PDF pp. 68–74: complete cubic interpolation and its error argument.

contents.name: Chapter X BVALUE: span localization, local B-spline coefficient reduction, and the final order-one value
contents.reason: The algorithm uses the same local reduction. Its exact value identity and arithmetic count are proved from the repository's Cox–de Boor recurrence, and its floating-point bound is proved separately under the published operationwise model.

contents.name: Chapter XI knot insertion: one inserted knot, local control blends, and unchanged spline curve
contents.reason: The source supplies the one-knot control and basis refinement formulas; the local basis identity is proved in the new A-page lemma, then the preservation theorem collects the updated control coefficients.

contents.name: Chapter XI single-knot basis refinement identity
contents.reason: The chapter gives the one-knot B-spline refinement relation; the local carrier proves its degree-by-degree form by induction from the repository recurrence, including repeated knots and half-open endpoints.

contents.name: Chapter XI single-knot control update and affine blend weights
contents.reason: The procedure records the source's one-new-knot case with explicit zero-based indexing and admissible non-knot insertion input.

contents.name: Chapter IV complete/clamped endpoint slopes and natural endpoint-curvature boundary choice
contents.reason: The source distinguishes prescribed endpoint slopes from natural zero-curvature endpoints; the local definition keeps those boundary conditions separate.

contents.name: Chapter IV natural boundary conditions and their endpoint approximation caveat
contents.reason: The local example directly computes the x-squared natural interpolant and its nonzero endpoint-adjacent error; no natural fourth-order rate is imported.

contents.name: Chapter V complete cubic spline interpolation error and its proof route
contents.reason: The source independently treats exact endpoint-slope interpolation. The item proves its stated nonuniform-mesh bound locally by the second-derivative system, a diagonal-dominance estimate and cubic Hermite remainders; no sharper source constant is claimed.

contents.name: Chapter XI convex-hull property for exact B-spline coefficient blends
contents.reason: Only exact convex-combination structure is used. The finite-precision statement and its range qualifications are derived locally and are not attributed to the geometric convex-hull property.

contents.name: Chapter IV natural-cubic system, cubic pieces, and endpoint conventions
contents.locator: Chapter IV, printed pp. 43–45 / PDF pp. 60–62
contents.reason: The source supplies the exact natural-spline setting and piece construction. The local certificate separately accounts for rounded system assembly and uses the proved residual-transfer supplier; no natural fourth-order claim is imported.

sources.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation
sources.locator: Complete 39-page lecture-note PDF fetched and inspected. Relevant range: §§1.1.1–1.1.4 and 1.2.1, PDF pp. 1–14: knot sequences, Cox–de Boor recursion, half-open/zero-denominator conventions, support, smoothness and the Curry–Schoenberg B-spline basis theorem.

contents.name: Definitions 1–2 and Examples 3–4: knot sequence, degree-zero indicators, Cox–de Boor recurrence and repeated-knot conventions
contents.reason: These conventions are incorporated explicitly in the local algorithm and its proof; the library's own published definition remains the canonical supplier.

contents.name: Theorem 11: B-spline support, smoothness and recurrence consequences
contents.reason: The current published supplier already proves the support and repeated-knot properties used by the local de Boor claim.

contents.name: Theorem 13: Curry–Schoenberg B-spline basis for the spline space
contents.reason: The published basis theorem is reused; this batch does not restate or broaden its spline-space scope.

contents.name: §1.2.4 Theorem 21: explicit B-spline representation functionals
contents.reason: The assigned exact coefficient evaluation uses the local recurrence and does not need derivative-based B-spline coefficient recovery or a new representation-functional item.

sources.title: Brian LeMesurier, Introduction to Numerical Methods and Analysis with Python, Chapter 3.4
sources.locator: Complete Chapter 3.4 page fetched and read. Relevant §§3.4.1–3.4.3, lines 142–238: cubic pieces from nodal second derivatives, natural tridiagonal system, clamped endpoint slopes, and Theorem 3.5's clamped fourth-order error statement.

contents.name: §3.4.1 equations (3.5)–(3.8): cubic pieces, slope matching and the natural tridiagonal system
contents.reason: The canonical natural interpolation system and piece formula are already published and inspected; this batch reuses them without redefining the natural method.

contents.name: §3.4.2 equation (3.10): exact derivative boundary conditions for clamped interpolation
contents.reason: The local definition specifies both endpoint slopes and separately proves the variable-mesh tridiagonal system.

contents.name: §3.4.3 Theorem 3.5: maximum-norm fourth-order error for exact clamped derivatives
contents.reason: The theorem supports the scope. The local proof establishes its own explicit bound, 83/324 times M H^4, for arbitrary positive mesh widths.

contents.name: §3.4.3 natural-spline error paragraph following Theorem 3.5
contents.reason: The paragraph is not used as a premise. The assigned plan requires the natural endpoint caveat, and the local x-squared calculation checks it directly; no natural fourth-order f-fourth-derivative claim is imported.

contents.name: §3.4.1 natural tridiagonal system and cubic reconstruction; §3.4.3 boundary-error caveat
contents.reason: The source independently records the exact natural system, piece formula, and endpoint caveat. The local proof derives the rounded forward bound from its own successful residual certificate and exact assembly discrepancies.

contents.name: Triangular substitution recurrences, factorization context, and operation count
contents.reason: These sections provide an independent full-text treatment of the underlying factor and solve procedures. The band specialization, arithmetic statuses, and linear work are specified and proved locally.

contents.name: Cholesky factorization and backward-versus-forward error analysis
contents.reason: The notes support the distinction between a factor/solve residual and a forward bound. The exact successful-call bounds here are derived from the repository's proved rounded suppliers, not attributed to the notes.
